CHH1.label: D-ac36b6

defects.summary: S33 reads the card's HTML through pageTree instead of running the page through runPageHtml as the plan asks, and so drops 'read off the RUNNING page;' from the exact test name; the change is recorded in §12 item 10, and the assertions do cover the Then (cooldown-line, badge and title, no reset-line with a snapshot that would draw one, the other card unchanged).

ReadResetAsync decides explicit or undecided from the reason text containing 'Individual quota reached', not from the outcome's Spent field, so a text-classified (Spent == null) agy refusal that holds the sentence is parked on stated/guess even when the gauge reads Available; this is recorded as deviation 9 but differs from D5's undecided rule.

AfterRoundAsync catches OperationCanceledException around the whole DecideAsync, so one cancelled agy probe also throws away decisions already made for other keys in the same round (for example a Claude spend-limit park).
S35 and S36 depend on a 150 ms Task.Delay so that writer B reaches the lock before A releases it; if B starts late, an unlocked implementation could still pass, so the red depends on timing.
S7 sets Attempts = 1 on the outcome itself before it calls ReviewerSummaryFactory.Describe, so the 'rate limited (after 1 attempt)' prefix is not proved for the launch as the executor returns it.

AgyError.Parse also reads pretty-printed AGY_ERROR blocks over several lines by trying to parse up to 40 growing prefixes, which goes beyond D2's 'every line starting AGY_ERROR' and is not in the §12 deviation list.

CHH1.summary: Build, both suites and format are green; 42 of 43 scenarios pass under their exact names, and the 43rd (S33) is a recorded rename that still asserts its Then. D1–D11 are delivered faithfully: the structured spent verdict, the table-keyed agy groups, the /quota reader with its edge cases, the locked fail-open cooldown file with its refusal notice, per-key aggregation, roster and security-lane exclusion, the wire member and the card. The deviations are honest and recorded, and only minor findings on test timing and small spec drift remain.

CHH1.label: D-3e5d1f

defects.summary: The plan says S33 must run the page through runPageHtml. This test reads the static card HTML with pageTree and drops 'read off the RUNNING page' from the test name; deviation 10 records this, so the exact-name check counts S33 as absent.
The new status line says the plan text below is 'as it was frozen', but D5's paragraph on what `consecutive` means was rewritten in place, so that sentence is not true.

ReadResetAsync finds an explicit refusal by searching the reason text for 'Individual quota reached' instead of reading the outcome's Spent field, so a refusal found only by the text scan that contains that sentence (no AGY_ERROR line) is parked even when the gauge reads Available (deviation 9 records this).
S7 sets Attempts = 1 by hand before it calls Describe, so the 'rate limited (after 1 attempt)' prefix does not come from the real launch path.

To read pretty-printed lines, OfBlock parses each longer run of lines again (up to 40 JSON parses for each marker) in one dense LINQ expression, which is more clever than the plan's line reader needs.
S35 and S36 use a 150 ms Task.Delay to make B contend for the lock while A holds it, so 'B waited' is likely but the test does not prove it deterministically.

Several edits are outside the plan's scope list (the Rounds-block row, ConsultFailures reading Spent, the security-lane sentence, the DeepSeek and custom-codex keys); §12 records each one with a sound reason, but together they make the change larger.

CHH1.summary: The build and both suites are green, and 42 of 43 scenarios pass under their exact names; the 43rd, S33, exists under a shorter name and reads the static HTML instead of running the page. D1–D12 are implemented faithfully, with a locked, fail-open cooldown file, per-key aggregation, the measured agy table, and the server and card halves; the findings are all minor: a few recorded deviations, one untrue status sentence, and some dense or timing-based code.

CHH2.label: D-da0248

defects.summary: Separate `claude+key`/`codex+key` quota keys were added beyond D3/D9: a second `QuotaKeyOf(model, apiKey)` interface overload, plus a check that reads any environment variable ending in `_API_KEY`. The read side (`PanelService.CoolingOf`, which looks at the vault) and the write side (`AfterRoundAsync`, which looks at the launch environment) use two different checks, and those checks must stay in step; this is recorded as deviation 12.
`ConsultFailures.Classify` now reads `Spent`, although D12 puts the consultation roads out of scope; this is recorded as deviation 13.

Any `Ok` on a keyed row makes a `LiftDecision`, so almost every round takes the cross-process lock synchronously (it can wait up to 30 s) even when nothing is parked. If the lock is busy, this gives a server notice that says a cooldown was not recorded, for a lift that had nothing to remove.
The new implementation-status line was added above the old status line, which still says 'plan only, nothing implemented yet', so the head of the plan contradicts itself.

The DoD requires each scenario to be seen red first. S28, S30 and S38 were never seen red, and the break-it runs for S6, S8 and S27 were not done. The plan says this openly, but the DoD item is still not met.
S33 calls `runPageHtml` but makes its assertions on the static tree parsed from the drawn HTML, not on the page after its script ran, so 'read off the RUNNING page' is met only loosely.
A 150-line hand-written brace and string scanner reads multi-line AGY_ERROR objects, where a `Utf8JsonReader` reading one value after the marker would be smaller.

`RateLimited` detects HTTP 429 by checking that the sentence built by `WhyItFailed` ends with '(HTTP 429)', instead of reading `api_error_status` directly. This ties the check to the wording of a display string.
In S40, the `FractionAboveOne` row cannot tell a skipped bucket from one that was read, and the theory compares verdicts by their `ToString()`.

CHH2.summary: All 43 scenarios exist and pass, and build, both suites and format are green. The decisions are carried out faithfully: the three-valued `Spent`, the agy and /quota readers with the measured table and edge cases, the locked fail-open cooldown file, per-key aggregation with one probe per key, the roster exclusion, the wire member and the card. Each place where the plan contradicts itself (the S25 date, S34 against S41) is resolved soundly and recorded. The marks go down for scope additions beyond the plan (separate API-key quota keys, the consult classifier), some extra machinery, gaps in the red-first DoD (disclosed in the plan), and a plan status line that contradicts itself.

defects.summary: One cancelled agy probe ends the whole DecidedAsync loop, so the round also loses the park or lift it had already decided for other keys (codex, claude, kimi), not only the agy key.

An undecided agy refusal asks /quota only when the word scan already calls it hopeless (Qualifies), so an undecided RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED without spent words (possible in the older code/message shape) never reaches the gauge, but D5 says the gauge decides the undecided agy case.

S33 runs the page with runPageHtml but throws the result away and asserts on the parsed static tree, but the plan and PROJECT.md's webview rule ask for the line and badge to be read off the RUNNING page.
The new implementation status line was added above the old 'plan only, nothing implemented yet' status, and the old line was not changed, so the header now says two different things.

A second QuotaKeyOf(model, apiKey) overload, the +key keys and an env-name heuristic (RunsOnApiKey) are added beyond D3; this is recorded as deviation 12, but it widens the interface and keeps two different ways (env vs vault) to decide the same fact.
A hand-written brace and quote scanner (about 100 lines plus a new CA1502 section) reads the multi-line AGY_ERROR object; a JSON reader that stops after one value would do the same with less code.
TellOnce gives a notice on every refused write, not once, so its name says something the code does not do.
The CLAUDE_SPEND envelope is copied into a new constant instead of reusing AClaudeReasonInItsEnvelopeTests.SpendLimit, and the Edited/Bucket/Sink test helpers are copied between two test classes.
Left() writes the rounded-up time-left rule again on the C# side, a second copy of the rule in resetWords.ts.

CHH2.summary: The build, both suites and format are green, and all 43 scenarios are present and pass; the code delivers D1–D12 faithfully: the three-valued verdict, the agy readers, the table, a locked fail-open file, the per-key aggregation after the round, the roster exclusion, the wire member and the card. Every deviation (S25's date, S34's undecided row, API-key keys, reds not seen) is recorded honestly in §12; what remains is minor: cancellation scope, a test that does not read the running page, a stale status line, and some extra or duplicated code.

CHH3.label: D-d8154b

defects.summary: One test fails in the full MCP run (ATakeWhoseStreamCannotBeMade_ClosesItsDescriptor_AndLeavesTheFileFree, failedNew in objective.json), so the suite is red on this host; the most likely cause is a parallel test that starts a child process (the new end-to-end test starts git) and inherits the descriptor, which is not closed on exec, but the change still leaves the suite red.

If the re-read under the lock fails with IOException or UnauthorizedAccessException, Read() returns an empty list, and the write that follows then replaces the file with only this round's entries, so it can remove parks that another process wrote; the write path should refuse instead of failing open.

DecidedUnlessCancelled catches only OperationCanceledException, so any other exception from one key's ReadResetAsync escapes to the catch-all in AfterRoundAsync, and the parks and lifts already decided for every other key in the round are lost.
ReadResetAsync (a switch with seven arms and guards) and CooldownSentences.QuotaName (eight arms) go above the story rule of cyclomatic complexity ≤ 4 per method.
The new file src_mcp/src/Server/CooldownSentences.cs and the export of spanOf from resetWords.ts are outside the plan's file list, and §12 does not record them.

The AGY_1_3_3 reason constant is defined again here and also in QuotaFixtures; the same ISO-UTC format is also written three times (CooldownSentences.Iso, CooldownInstantConverter and the note in AntigravityRuntime).

CHH3.summary: All 43 scenario tests exist and pass, and the code follows the plan closely: a three-valued Spent field, the agy error reader for both shapes, an exact bucket-id table, /quota parsing with the plan's edge cases, a locked durable file that fails open with refusals reported out loud, per-key aggregation after the round, roster exclusion with this side's sentence, and the card line and badge; §12 records the deviations, and the ones checked are true (for example, S3's planned red cannot happen while ResetOutlasts is unchanged). The score is lower because one other MCP test fails in the full run, there are small robustness gaps in the write path and the aggregation, and a few methods break the plan's complexity rule.

CHH3.label: D-d5b6b4

defects.summary: The full MCP suite is red on this host: ATakeWhoseStreamCannotBeMade_ClosesItsDescriptor_AndLeavesTheFileFree fails although it passes at the start commit. The cause is most likely a fork race with its in-host inheritable descriptor, because the new round integration test starts real git children, but every new failure counts.
The file has 408 lines, and the story card says to split it into two files past 400 lines; this is not recorded in the §12 deviations.
S35 and S36 depend on a 300 ms Task.Delay for writer B to reach the lock while A holds it. If B starts later, the test still passes but does not show that B waited.
SpendLimitSentence parses the envelope again with its own try/catch, a copy of WhyItFailed's parse, when it could reuse that read and add only the 429 check.
The AGY_1_3_3 reason string is copied here as Agy133Reason and again in QuotaFixtures.Agy133Reason, when the shared fixture class could hold the only copy.

CHH3.summary: The change delivers all four stories as the plan says: a three-valued Spent verdict, an AGY_ERROR reader for both shapes, the measured agy key table with Argon on its own key, a /quota reader with every edge case, a locked durable cooldown file that fails open and refuses writes out loud, per-key aggregation after the round, roster exclusion with this side's sentence, the providers wire member and the card line and badge. All 43 scenarios exist and pass, and the plan's deviations (§12) are true and give their reasons. The main mark against it is one new failure in the full MCP suite, in an unrelated HeldFile test that is probably a race; the other findings are small (file size, a timing-based interleave test, a few duplicates).
